about:
Burmeister Woodwork Co. operates from Hales Corners, Wisconsin, tracing its roots to the early 1920s when Marvin Burmeister founded Advance Millwork. The company adopted its current name in 1937 and remained family-owned through three generations—George Burmeister took over in 1964, adding stair fabrication, and his son Russell shifted focus to high-end architectural millwork in 1981. In 2015, John Sprenger, a military veteran, purchased the business and now serves as president, emphasizing a culture of craftsmanship he attributes to his service experience.

The firm produces custom architectural millwork—cabinetry, stairs, moldings, doors, and related components—for luxury residential and commercial projects. A 40,000-square-foot manufacturing facility houses a team of 60 professionals who combine traditional hand craftsmanship with modern engineering, fabrication, finishing, and installation capabilities. The shop collaborates with specialty vendors to integrate custom veneers, exotic wood species, metal, glass, and upholstery into complex, technically demanding projects.

Clients span the luxury residential sector and commercial interiors across the Midwest and nationally. Representative projects include a modern bank lobby, historic stable conversion, Chicago greystone renovation, penthouse interiors, and a boat enthusiast’s dream residence, illustrating the range from contemporary urban spaces to rustic lake-country homes.

Sprenger cites the pursuit of excellence learned in the military as a driving force, and the company positions its 89-year legacy as a foundation for delivering uncompromising artisanship on each project.
